description: Atom serial number (file-based). Unique for each atom in the molecule.
Residue index (0-based). Internal index for each residue.
Residue sequence number using author-defined numbering. For PDB files, this is the
residue sequence number from the ATOM record columns 23-26. For CIF files, this
corresponds to auth_seq_id (the author's original numbering, which may contain gaps).
This follows the ProDy convention, where resid/resnum always refers to the author's
numbering. To access the CIF-internal sequential numbering (label_seq_id, which
restarts at 1 for each entity), use the 'label_seq_id' keyword instead.
See also: label_seq_id, auth_seq_id, residue.
CIF-internal residue sequence number (label_seq_id). 1-based, restarts at 1 for
each entity/chain. Only available for CIF-format structures; PDB files do not have
this field. Note: this was previously a synonym of resid but was separated because
label_seq_id and auth_seq_id can differ significantly (e.g. in multi-chain CIF files
where label_seq_id restarts per chain but auth_seq_id is globally unique).
See also: resid, auth_seq_id, residue.
Chain identifier (file-based). Single-letter code distinguishing subcomponents of a molecule.
Model number (file-based). Used for multi-model structures (e.g., NMR ensembles).
Atom index (0-based). Internal index for each atom.
Chain index (0-based). Usually identifies connected fragments (e.g., protein chains, nucleic acid chains).
Model number (0-based). Used for animation frames or trajectory steps.
Atom name. Standard chemical nomenclature (e.g., 'CA' for alpha carbon).
Residue name. Three-letter code (e.g., 'GLY' for glycine).
Record name. Used to distinguish record types in structure files.
Code for insertion of residues. Used for residue insertion codes in PDB files.
Alternate location indicator. Used for alternate conformations of atoms.

x.short: Orthogonal coordinates for X in Angstroms.
description: Orthogonal coordinates for X in Angstroms. Static position of the atom.

y.short: Orthogonal coordinates for Y in Angstroms.
description: Orthogonal coordinates for Y in Angstroms. Static position of the atom.

z.short: Orthogonal coordinates for Z in Angstroms.
description: Orthogonal coordinates for Z in Angstroms. Static position of the atom.
Occupancy. Fractional occupancy of the atom position.
Temperature factor (B-factor). Atomic displacement parameter.
Charge on the atom. Partial or formal charge.
Element symbol. Chemical element (e.g., 'C', 'O', 'N').
Segment name. Groups atoms into functional substructures (e.g., protein, water).
Atom type. Used for parameterization or classification (e.g., force field types).
Mass. Atomic mass, used for dynamics and analysis.
Atomic number (0 if undefined).

bonds.short: Number of bonds this atom participates in.
description: Number of bonds this atom participates in.
Atom radius. Used for visualization and analysis.

anisotropy.short: Standard deviations for anisotropic temperature factor.
description: Standard deviations for anisotropic temperature factor (e.g., 'type CT1 CT2 CT3').
Velocity in the x direction. Used in dynamics/trajectories.
Velocity in the y direction. Used in dynamics/trajectories.
Velocity in the z direction. Used in dynamics/trajectories.
Force in the x direction. Used in dynamics/trajectories.
Force in the y direction. Used in dynamics/trajectories.
Force in the z direction. Used in dynamics/trajectories.

ufx.short: Force to apply in the x coordinate.
description: Force to apply in the x coordinate (external or user-applied).

ufy.short: Force to apply in the y coordinate.
description: Force to apply in the y coordinate (external or user-applied).

ufz.short: Force to apply in the z coordinate.
description: Force to apply in the z coordinate (external or user-applied).
Secondary structure assignment (e.g., 'H' for helix, 'E' for strand).
Backbone phi angle. Main chain dihedral angle in proteins.
Backbone psi angle. Main chain dihedral angle in proteins.
Author-defined chain identifier (as published).
Author-defined atom name (as published).
Author-defined residue name (as published).
Author-defined residue sequence number as published in the CIF file. For CIF
structures, this is identical to what resid returns (since resid uses author
numbering). For PDB files, this column is not present (resid already contains
the author numbering directly). Provided for explicit CIF field access.
See also: resid, label_seq_id.
Protein fragment index.
Nucleic fragment index.
